PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fix SSH and WSL relay reuse on reconnect
PullRequest.Body:
agentHost: fix SSH and WSL relay reuse on reconnect

Keep protocol clients and their initialized transports together. Give each new protocol client a
fresh relay to prevent the "Method not found: initialize" error on repeated connections.

- Reuse connected SSH and WSL clients and join concurrent connection requests.
- Replace retained relays before a new protocol client starts its handshake.
- Keep the SSH session and selected endpoint when replacing its relay.
- Release old transport resources without closing the replacement connection.
- Add regression tests for repeated connects, retained relays, recovery, and resource cleanup.

Validation: 590 unit tests passed, along with client typecheck, transpilation, targeted ESLint, and
git diff --check. Native SSH and WSL end-to-end validation remains outstanding.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335919

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The retention and nested traversal follow directly from the added map write and prune implementation. User reconnect counts vary, but the growth mechanism and complexity are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained map entries and string UUIDs, plus synchronous map traversal CPU during relay release
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After R successful reconnects on a long-lived host, `_replacements` retains O(R) aliases. `_releaseRelay` calls `_pruneReplacements`, which iterates all aliases and `_getCurrentLease` walks each remaining chain, making a renewal perform O(R²) map lookups in the worst case.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Retained memory and progressively increasing shared-process CPU/reconnect latency during network churn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: SSH reconnect reused the stable connection key and retained no historical relay-ID chain.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every successful renewal retains a predecessor-to-successor UUID in `_replacements` for the lifetime of the current relay chain.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_replacements.set(expectedConnectionId, result.connectionId)` creates one durable historical alias per successful reconnect; no equivalent state existed before this diff.
Findings.Title: Bound SSH relay replacement history
Findings.Impact: A long-lived SSH agent connection that repeatedly recovers from network changes accumulates every old relay ID; later reconnects synchronously rescan increasingly long chains before recovery completes.
Findings.Evidence: Line 1173 appends `oldId -> newId`. `_pruneReplacements` keeps every alias while its chain reaches the live lease, and `_getCurrentLease` follows successor links one by one. Entries are removed only when the final chain no longer resolves or the entire session closes, so successful renewals do not bound the history.
Findings.Recommendation: Use `_pendingReconnects` for in-flight coalescing, then remove the superseded ID once callers have adopted the result; if stale lookup must remain, path-compress it to a bounded direct alias and explicitly expire old aliases.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed map write, chain walker, and prune condition prove linear retention and quadratic worst-case pruning. Only the number of reconnects in typical sessions is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained UUID strings/map entries and synchronous map traversal CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With R successful recoveries in one long-lived distro session, the map holds O(R) IDs. Every `_closeRelay` invokes `_pruneReplacements`; it scans all aliases and calls `_getCurrentRelay`, which can traverse O(R) links for each key, producing O(R²) lookup work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded per-session memory growth and progressively slower relay replacement/cleanup.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: WSL reconnect replaced the single connection directly and retained no predecessor alias map.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successful WSL relay renewal adds another old-to-new connection ID that remains reachable while the current lease lives.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_replacements.set(expectedConnectionId, result.connectionId)` introduces one retained alias per successful reconnect; the base implementation had no replacement-history structure.
Findings.Title: Bound WSL relay replacement history
Findings.Impact: On a flaky network or repeatedly suspended machine, a WSL agent that successfully reconnects many times keeps all prior relay IDs and spends increasing shared-process time pruning them on subsequent recoveries.
Findings.Evidence: The changed line records `expectedConnectionId -> result.connectionId`. `_pruneReplacements` deliberately retains aliases whenever `_getCurrentRelay` can reach the current lease, so every predecessor in a successful chain survives until final session teardown.
Findings.Recommendation: Drop the old alias after the coalesced reconnect promise has handed out the new ID, or retain only a bounded/path-compressed direct alias with explicit expiry for late callers.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed catch, session close listener, expensive reconnect path, and multi-lease test establish the mechanism. The only uncertainty is how often a relay channel fails independently of an otherwise usable SSH session.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SSH connections and exec channels, remote endpoint-discovery commands, relay sockets, and renderer IPC reconnect work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The failure closes one lease per active renderer on the host. The next session setup is coalesced, but it still performs one full SSH handshake/discovery sequence and then creates a replacement relay for each affected renderer.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A per-channel failure causes cross-window reconnect latency, extra SSH/network traffic, and a burst of relay recreation.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An existing-host connect returned the existing connection and created no additional relay; reconnect replaced the sole relay, so failure of a newly requested lease could not fan out to multiple active clients.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Any failed relay lease acquisition now disposes the shared SSH session, which disposes all sibling leases and forces all renderers to recover.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `session.dispose();` at line 1282 converts one `_createRelayLease` failure into disposal of the shared session introduced by this diff.
Findings.Title: Do not drop every SSH window on one failed relay acquisition
Findings.Impact: If a new window or one reconnecting client hits a transient `forwardOut`/relay error while sibling leases are healthy, all windows lose their relays. Recovery redoes `_connectSSH`, remote `uname` calls, CLI installation checks, and endpoint discovery before those windows can proceed.
Findings.Evidence: The new catch unconditionally calls `session.dispose()`. `SSHConnection.onDidClose` then removes and disposes every lease for that session and fires close events. `_connect` proves the replacement critical path includes `_connectSSH`, two remote `uname` execs, `_ensureCLIInstalled`, and `runAgentEndpoints`. The added regression test for a failed lease renewal expects both existing lease IDs to close and a second SSH client/discovery pass.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the shared SSH session and sibling leases alive when only one relay creation fails; dispose the session only when there are no live leases or a bounded session-level health check confirms the SSH connection itself is unusable.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The fanout and subprocess restart are direct in the changed call path and asserted by the new test. Only the frequency of transient per-relay failures while sibling sockets remain healthy is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: WSL subprocess launches, WebSocket connections, IPC close/reconnect notifications, and remote CLI bootstrap work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The failure fans out across the number of active renderer leases for the distro. Session creation is coalesced to one bootstrap, but every affected renderer then performs recovery and acquires its own replacement relay.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A transient per-relay open failure can interrupt all windows and put a full WSL platform probe and agent-host bootstrap on their recovery critical path.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An already-live distro connect returned the existing connection and did not open another WebSocket; reconnect owned the single connection, so one new client could not evict multiple healthy clients.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A failed WebSocket acquisition for one lease now closes the shared distro session, which closes every other lease and kills the shared bootstrap process.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `this._closeSession(session.distro, session);` runs for any `_createRelay` exception, even when other entries in `_connections` still reference a working shared session.
Findings.Title: Do not restart every WSL client when one relay dial fails
Findings.Impact: When another window connects or one client renews while existing leases are healthy, a single `_openWebSocket` rejection closes all active sockets and kills the child; the next recovery runs `wsl.exe` platform detection and respawns the agent host, delaying every attached window.
Findings.Evidence: `connect` now shares one `IWSLSession` but creates an independent relay per caller. The added catch at line 480 calls `_closeSession`; that method iterates all leases, closes them, and kills `session.child`. `_connectUnguarded` shows recovery invokes `_resolvePlatform` (`wsl.exe`) and `_spawnAgentHost`. The added test explicitly expects a WebSocket-open failure on an existing session to close both leases, kill the old child, and spawn a second child.
Findings.Recommendation: Reject and clean up only the failed lease while other live leases remain; close/rebootstrap the shared session only on child/session failure or after a bounded health check establishes that the shared endpoint is dead.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and repeated SSH connection to one remote host across renderer clients
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold request must resolve SSH configuration, establish SSH, probe platform, ensure the CLI, discover/select an endpoint, and create a relay before protocol initialization. A warm request reuses the shared SSH session but still creates an independent relay. Renderer-local duplicate requests are coalesced before this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold host session after `_pendingSessions` grouping; zero for warm session reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold SSH connection already established one SSH session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remote `uname`, CLI installation checks, endpoint discovery, and possible standalone spawn over SSH exec
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped sequence per cold host session; no repeat for a healthy warm shared session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold bootstrap operations existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks endpoint selection and initial relay acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create WebSocket relay through the selected SSH endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per effective renderer client; simultaneous windows can acquire relays concurrently after sharing one SSH session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repeated connects to an existing host returned the same relay result instead of allocating independent relay leases.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Relay messages and lifecycle events between renderer and shared process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical channel per effective client, with message cardinality driven by protocol traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relay IPC existed, but duplicate clients could share the same connection identifier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Carries all protocol traffic after connection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of renderer windows connecting to the same SSH host; one relay is required per effective renderer protocol client after renderer-side coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `_pendingSessions` coalesces SSH session creation per connection key, while callers awaiting that session invoke `_acquireRelay` independently and may create relays concurrently. `_pendingConnections` coalesces same-renderer connects and `_pendingReconnects` coalesces renewals for one expected lease.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A live `_connections` session is the positive cache. SSH config resolution also has time-bounded reuse. Failed session creation is removed from `_pendingSessions`, so retries are not negatively cached. Warm connects avoid SSH/platform/discovery work but not per-client relay creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: grouping, relay multiplicity, and critical-path boundaries are explicit in the implementation and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent window count is usually small, so the necessary per-client relay burst was not separately reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: The shared-session/coalescing design avoids duplicate SSH bootstraps. Independent relays are required for protocol isolation; no report was made for their normal creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: SSH relay renewal or additional-client relay acquisition fails while sibling leases are active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The failed caller awaits relay creation. The changed catch then performs diagnostic endpoint work, disposes the shared session, closes every sibling lease, and moves all affected renderers onto recovery; the first recovery must complete a full cold SSH bootstrap before any client can resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing-host connects reused the sole result, so a newly requested sibling relay could not fail and fan out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Diagnostic remote endpoint read after relay failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per failed acquisition, timeout-bounded; skipped on relay timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relay failure diagnostics already reread endpoint state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the failure is surfaced and session disposal completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full SSH handshake and remote discovery after shared-session disposal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced cold session bootstrap, followed by one relay per affected renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One relay failure did not fan out across multiple independently leased clients because those leases did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All sibling clients closed by the failure wait on this recovery path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active renderer leases on the same SSH session, plus reconnect history length for that session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session re-creation is grouped by `_pendingSessions`, but all affected renderers can schedule recovery and then acquire independent replacement relays concurrently. One expected lease's renewal is coalesced by `_pendingReconnects`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The relay failure invalidates the positive shared-session cache unconditionally, even when sibling leases remain. A subsequent session is cold; there is no negative cache. Historical replacement IDs remain cached in `_replacements` until the final current lease/session disappears.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unconditional `session.dispose`, all-lease close propagation, and the cold bootstrap path are directly traced and covered by a test expecting both leases to close.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Independent per-channel failures may be uncommon; when they occur, the number of attached windows and remote bootstrap duration determine severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fanout: one per-lease error invalidates shared healthy work and forces cross-window remote recovery. Replacement aliases also grow with every successful renewal and make pruning progressively more expensive.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and repeated WSL connection to one distro across renderer clients
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold request checks platform via WSL, composes and spawns the agent-host bootstrap, waits for its URL, then opens a WebSocket relay. Warm requests reuse the shared session/child but open one independent relay per effective renderer client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `wsl.exe` command per cold distro session after grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold WSL connects already performed platform detection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn WSL agent-host bootstrap, including possible CLI preparation/download
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per cold distro session after `_pendingConnects` grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold connects already spawned the bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks until the child prints its WebSocket URL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open local WebSocket relay to the WSL agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per effective renderer client; simultaneous callers can open sockets concurrently after sharing one bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An existing distro returned the existing connection instead of allocating a separate relay.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Relay protocol messages and close/activity notifications
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical IPC relay per effective client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relay IPC existed with a single distro-scoped connection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of renderer windows attached to one distro after renderer-local connect coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `_pendingConnects` coalesces one WSL bootstrap per distro. Once available, callers create WebSocket relays independently. Renderer `_pendingConnections` joins same-window requests and upgrades a pending background request rather than launching a second factory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `_sessions` is a positive live-session cache and `_pendingConnects` coalesces cold creation. Failures clear pending state and are retried; no negative cache is retained. Warm clients reuse the child and URL.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: bootstrap grouping and per-client relay behavior are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The normal added relay count equals active renderer clients and is necessary for isolation; realistic simultaneous window counts are limited.
Scenarios.Verdict: Normal warm reuse and same-renderer coalescing are performance-positive; required independent relay allocation was not reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: WSL relay renewal or additional-client WebSocket open fails while sibling leases are active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One `_openWebSocket` failure enters the changed catch, closes the shared session, closes every sibling socket, kills the WSL bootstrap child, and sends all attached renderers into recovery. The next caller must rerun platform detection and respawn the bootstrap before any replacement relay can initialize.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Failed local WebSocket open for one requested relay
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A connect to an already-live distro returned the existing connection and did not perform another WebSocket open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rejects the caller and, through session closure, blocks every sibling client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child kill per failed shared session, with a possible SIGKILL escalation timer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A newly requested sibling relay could not kill a shared multi-lease session because that model did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Guarantees the next recovery cannot use warm bootstrap state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rerun WSL platform probe and agent-host bootstrap
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced bootstrap after the fanout, then one WebSocket per affected renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Additional connects reused the existing connection and did not force this cross-client recovery path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All closed clients wait for this cold work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active renderer leases on the distro, and number of successful recoveries retained in the replacement chain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold rebootstrap is coalesced per distro, while each affected renderer subsequently creates its own relay. One expected connection ID's reconnect is coalesced by `_pendingReconnects`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The failure unconditionally evicts the live session cache. Recovery is cold with no negative cache. `_replacements` retains every successful predecessor alias while the current relay remains reachable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed catch, session close loop, child kill, and test expecting two lease closes and a second child prove the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of WebSocket-open failures while existing sockets remain usable and the number of attached windows are workload-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fanout. Separately, replacement aliases are retained for the full live chain, causing O(R) memory and O(R²) worst-case pruning after R successful recoveries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over all 15 changed files and all diff pages. Reported four issues: failed lease acquisition tears down every shared SSH/WSL client and forces cold recovery, and both replacement maps retain unbounded historical ID chains with quadratic worst-case pruning. Normal session coalescing, per-client relay allocation, cleanup ownership, caches, and concurrency were also traced; no concrete performance-regression fix suitable for blame learning was established.
